Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor, Sofia Alvarez (Redwood) - Raj Patel, Elena Torres, Samir Bhatt, Priya Singh (Nova Systems)

Auto-summary (auto-gen may be imperfect): Discussed three target accounts and where Nova and Redwood will split hunting motions, technical gating around Dedicated vs Hosted, and plan a 2-week micro-pilot for the top account.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - Maya from Redwood here, Liam our SE, Sofia on partner ops. Raj, Elena, you on?
[00:08] Raj Patel: Yep, I'm here. Hola. Raj on the Nova side. Elena is on - she just hopped on.
[00:13] Elena Torres: Hi all, good to meet.
[00:15] Liam O'Connor: Great. Quick agenda - prioritize three joint accounts, align pilot scope, and clear any technical blockers for Dedicated / private deploys.
[00:25] Samir Bhatt: Sounds good. One thing up front: our security team always asks for SOC2 and encryption details, and with these accounts they may require VPC peering or an on-prem option.
[00:35] Sofia Alvarez: Noted. We'll attach the security packet after. We support VPC and private control plane, plus KMS/HSM integration.
[00:42] Raj Patel: Awesome. For account prioritization, we have DeltaCorp (healthcare), Azurea (fintech), and Meridian (adtech). DeltaCorp is highest priority because of timing - RFP due early April.
[00:55] Maya Chen: Ok DeltaCorp as top. Quick qualification: is Delta doing on-prem requirement or will they accept VPC?
[01:03] Elena Torres: They prefer a private deployment — air-gapped conversation possible but likely a managed VPC into their cloud.
[01:10] Liam O'Connor: We can support managed VPC into their AWS tenant, Redwood Private with customer-managed network. There are some configuration steps for routing and certs but it's standard.
[01:22] Priya Singh: For procurement, Delta's legal also asked about audit logs retention and e-discovery. What's Redwood's retention window?
[01:29] Maya Chen: Default logs retention 90 days but enterprise options for longer retention are available as an add-on. We'll note that in the security packet.
[01:36] Raj Patel: Great. On the technical gating — Delta also wants latency under 120ms p50 for generation flows of ~256 tokens, with a throughput profile of 30 concurrent sessions. Is that realistic?
[01:48] Liam O'Connor: For a standard LLM, hitting p50 <120ms at 256 tokens with 30 conc sessions is tight on hosted single-tenant pools; Dedicated with optimized kernels and batching we can get there. We'll need to tune batching and optionally use quantized weights. There's also KV cache warmup considerations.
[02:05] Samir Bhatt: When you say quantized, do you mean we need to use an int8 profile? How does that affect quality?
[02:12] Liam O'Connor: Usually int8 or 4-bit can drop cost significantly, but there's a small quality delta depending on the model. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per workload and we'd run evals on your prompts to check regressions.
[02:25] Elena Torres: Ok, we need that eval to show no regression on our 50 prompt set.
[02:30] Maya Chen: We'll include that as a requirement in the micro-pilot scope.
[02:35] [02:35] Raj Patel: Next, who will run the pilot? Nova can provision customer contacts — we expect Redwood to provide a micro-benchmark plan and we'll loop in Delta's infra folks.
[02:45] Liam O'Connor: I'll draft a 2-week micro-benchmark: baseline run (hosted) vs dedicated rack, 5k requests simulated, payload sizes matching your production, measuring p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens.
[02:58] Priya Singh: Timeline question — Delta's RFP is early April, can we get benchmarks back by next Tuesday?
[03:05] Maya Chen: That's tight. We'll try. If we start the pilot this week we can have a preliminary report in 7 days. Finalized in two weeks.
[03:15] Raj Patel: Good. What about crediting for the co-sell? Nova wants clarity — who owns the logo, and how do we credit renewals?
[03:23] Maya Chen: Usually we run a co-sell agreement: Nova leads intro and first touch, Redwood owns contract for Dedicated/Private. For compensation, we'll map influenced revenue and a referral fee; we'll follow up with a short SOW template.
[03:36] Elena Torres: Can we get that template?
[03:38] Maya Chen: Yes, I'll share JD SOW and co-sell contact matrix after this call.
[03:43] [03:43] Samir Bhatt: Minor nit: our engineering team would like to see the net-new infra requirements. For dedicated we need to know GPU types and node counts.
[03:52] Liam O'Connor: For the performance target we suggest an initial 2-GPU rack using A800-equivalent, or AdaX variants; exact SKU depends on model choice. We'll include a rack-level config in the benchmark doc.
[04:05] Raj Patel: Competitors in their RFP include Vertex and an in-house model; Delta asked about offline evaluation against Anthropic. Any thoughts?
[04:13] Liam O'Connor: We can run apples-to-apples evals. But note that Anthropic results on safety benchmarks differ — we'll map both cost and safety tradeoffs.
[04:23] Priya Singh: On compliance: do you support customer-managed KMS?
[04:27] Maya Chen: Yes, KMS/HSM integrations are supported for Private and Dedicated. We'll include the integration guide in the packet.
[04:34] [04:34] Raj Patel: Ok next account Azurea — fintech — stricter controls and a long procurement cycle. We probably shouldn't push Dedicated here yet, maybe start with a hosted pilot.
[04:45] Maya Chen: That makes sense. Hosted to start, then migrate to Dedicated as needs grow. We can show a monetized path that highlights cost delta and regression checks.
[04:55] Elena Torres: Azurea will ask for egress controls and data residency in EU. Redwood have region-specific hosting?
[05:03] Liam O'Connor: Yes EU regions available, and we can pin model versions per region. Data residency options included in Private package.
[05:12] [05:12] Samir Bhatt: For Meridian (adtech) — lower security bar but high throughput and bursty traffic. Any recommendations?
[05:21] Liam O'Connor: For bursty workloads, smart routing + caching helps. Redwood's prefix KV cache can reduce repeated token cost; also adaptive batching to keep latency while improving cost. We'll demo caching patterns in the pilot.
[05:33] Maya Chen: Quick check — is there appetite to run three parallel micro-pilots or focus on Delta first?
[05:40] Raj Patel: Delta first, Azurea second if timings align. Meridian can be scoped later Q2.
[05:47] [05:47] Elena Torres: On pricing — Delta will want committed pricing for Dedicated. Do you offer reserved capacity?
[05:55] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Dedicated has reserved capacity contracts monthly/annual with burst options. We'll draft an indicative price for the pilot and a follow-on reserved model.
[06:05] Priya Singh: If we include reserved pricing in the proposal, procurement will likely push for SLAs. What SLA levels do you offer?
[06:12] Maya Chen: We have SLA tiers for Dedicated: uptime and latency SLOs can be included per contract. We'll provide sample SLA language.
[06:19] [06:19] Raj Patel: Security packet please. Also, can Redwood sign a data processing addendum?
[06:24] Maya Chen: Yes we have a DPA template. We'll include it in the packet.
[06:29] [06:29] Samir Bhatt: On the bench — do you need access to Delta's test dataset or can we use a sanitized prompt set?
[06:35] Liam O'Connor: Sanitized prompts are fine; for end-to-end infra metrics we might request traffic pattern replay or synthetic load matching their p50/p95 distributions.
[06:46] Raj Patel: Cool. Logistics: Raj will schedule pilot kickoff with Delta and loop infra. Maya to share GTM deck and security pack. Liam to prepare benchmark plan and initial rack config.
[06:58] Maya Chen: Confirming next steps: I'll send the joint GTM & co-sell matrix and SOW template; Liam will share benchmark template; Sofia will coordinate dates for kickoff.
[07:09] Priya Singh: One more ask — can Redwood provide a short one-page on model governance controls? Our legal wants to see safety guardrails.
[07:17] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we have a model governance one-pager. We'll include that.
[07:23] [07:23] Elena Torres: Any blockers from Redwood side for a deliverable by next Tuesday?
[07:28] Maya Chen: We can get a preliminary packet and benchmark template out by Monday, final benchmark run depends on kickoff timing.
[07:35] Raj Patel: Ok locking that in. If Delta's RFP is early April, we need to be fast.
[07:41] Maya Chen: Understood. Quick question — who is the internal champion at Delta?
[07:46] Raj Patel: We'll confirm, but it's likely Michael R. in AI initiatives. I'll include him in the kickoff.
[07:52] [07:52] Samir Bhatt: A quick technical aside: what monitoring hooks can we expose to the customer's observability? Traces, per-route latency?
[07:59] Liam O'Connor: Redwood Console exposes per-route dashboards, token-level cost, tracing hooks via OpenTelemetry, and audit logs. We'll show a demo screen in the pilot kickoff.
[08:11] [08:11] Priya Singh: Perfect. Last item — co-sell attribution. Raj and Maya, do we have an initial credit split?
[08:18] Maya Chen: We'll propose a referral fee + influenced revenue share for the first 12 months. Exact % to be in the co-sell deal template.
[08:27] Raj Patel: Fine.
[08:29] Maya Chen: Alright let's recap and close with concrete next steps.

- Maya: send joint GTM deck, SOW template, security packet (SOC2, ISO summary, DPA) by 2026-03-23/26.
